newsitem.title: USA: Apache, Seagull complete Egyptian wildcat.
newsitem.headline: Apache, Seagull complete Egyptian wildcat.

text.p: Apache Corp said Tuesday the Wadi El Rayan-1X exploratory well in Egypt has been completed after testing 950 barrels of 25-degree gravity oil daily.

The new field discovery, located in the southern portion of the Qarun concession in Egypt's Western Desert, was drilled 35 miles from the nearest established production, said Apache's partner there, Seagull Energy Corp.

Located about a mile north of the 6.8-million-acre East Beni Suef concession, Seagull's largest concession in Egypt, the wildcat establishes the southern-most production in the Western Desert, the company said.

Apache owns 75 percent of the contractor interest in the 1.9 million acre Qarun Concession and is operator of the contractor group. Seagull owns the remaining 25 percent. Qarun is operated by Qarun Petroleum Co, an Egyptian corporation owned jointly by the contractors and the Egyptian General Petroleum Corp, the national oil company.
Apache said "This discovery 35 miles south of the Qarun field opens up the potential of a new geologic trend for Apache in a new area of the Western Desert."
Seagull said the discovery is also "significant in that it raises expectations for the 6.8-million acre East Beni Suef concession to the south.
"Here, Seagull has a 50 percent working interest and will be the operator," with Apache holding the rest.

The Wadi El Rayan-1X is Apache's second oil discovery on the Qarun Concession in the last two months. The well was tested on a one-inch choke with 90 pounds per square inch of flowing tubing pressure from perforations between 5,550 feet and 5,716 feet in the Abu Roash "G" formation.

An appraisal well about two miles southwest of the discovery will commence within a few days and additional seismic data will be acquired over the next several months to evaluate structures similar to those encountered in the Wadi El Rayan-1X, the companies said.

Separately, Apache said that subsequent testing of its SW Qarun-1X discovery announced last week had boosted the well's official flow rate to 4,400 barrels of oil per day, up from 3,700 barrels per day in the earlier test reported October 1.
